name: Ovex DutyLine Security Trouser
description:
Straight-cut duty pants in charcoal or midnight navy, designed to look professional while carrying the weight of a full duty belt. Heavy-duty belt loops, two side cargo pockets, hidden shin pockets, and a structured waistband with internal stiffening. The fabric has a subtle sheen from its moisture-wicking finish.

Standard purchase for private security firms across Tiers 2 and 3. Some guards have worn the same pair for five years. Others buy them because they look vaguely official without being a uniform — useful for people who want to project authority without being affiliated.
functionality: Reinforced belt loops rated for full duty belt, hidden shin pockets, moisture-wicking finish, structured waistband
what_it_says: You work a post, you carry weight, and you've been doing it long enough to know what pants actually hold up.
story_hooks: A security guard realizes their hidden shin pockets were searched during a shift — by someone who knew exactly where to look.
The pants are sold in bulk to a private security firm that just lost a major contract — the guards are keeping them and looking for new work.

physical_description.visual_profile: Utilitarian straight-leg silhouette with a military-adjacent formality. Projects authority and readiness without screaming 'official uniform.' The fabric catches light subtly, suggesting technical functionality beneath a professional veneer.
physical_description.fit: Straight, unforgiving cut through hip and thigh. Sits high on waist with deliberate room in the seat for duty belt and gear. Tapers slightly at ankle without being slim. Built for standing eight-hour shifts, not comfort.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy-duty synthetic-wool blend with moisture-wicking treatment. Durable enough to handle repeated holstering, bending, and abrasion.
physical_description.texture: Tight, dense weave with slight sheen from technical finish. Crisp when new, develops subtle creasing at stress points (knees, hip folds) with wear. Resists wrinkling intentionally.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal or midnight navy. Matte base with reflective sheen only visible under direct light. No contrast stitching or logos—design language is aggressive minimalism.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty friction-fit waistband with internal stiffening bar. Standard zip fly. Reinforced button anchor point rated for loaded duty belt stress.
distinctive_features: Oversized belt loops (1.5" wide) designed for standard security belts
Two side cargo pockets with reinforced stitching and magnetic closures
Hidden shin pockets for backup mag or tactical knife
Internal waistband stiffener prevents sagging under gear weight
Subtle Ovex brand embossing at rear waistband (barely visible unless you know to look)
Reinforced crotch seam and thigh stress panels
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 functional. Expensive enough to signal serious duty (Φ400-550 retail), cheap enough for working-class security firms to outfit entire teams.
physical_description.cultural_context: Private security, corporate asset protection, off-duty law enforcement, and para-military contractors. Also worn by people who want 'authority aesthetic' without actual credentials—bouncers, nightclub staff, security theater players. The ambiguity is intentional.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in within months. Creases set at hip and knee. Faint scuffs from equipment. Some units show patina from five years of daily wear with minimal fading (quality dye-work). Never looks cheap, but never pristine after month two.
